blocks.explanation:
A fraction with squares on top and "sin cos" products below.
We must show it equals \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
Plan: top: \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\), then sum-to-product, giving \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\). Bottom: \(\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta\), then sum-to-product, giving \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha - \sin\beta\cos\beta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: Factorise, sum-to-product formulas and the double-angle formula \(2\sin u\cos u = \sin 2u\).

Numerator: difference of squares
\[\sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\]
\[= (\sin\alpha + \sin\beta)(\sin\alpha - \sin\beta)\]
Why: \(a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)\).

Each bracket as a product
\[\sin\alpha + \sin\beta = 2\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\]
\[\sin\alpha - \sin\beta = 2\cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\sin\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\]
Why: The \(\sin P \pm \sin Q\) formulas.

Regroup into double angles
\[\text{Num.} = \left(2\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)\times\]
\[\left(2\sin\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)\]
\[= \sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\]
Why: \(2\sin u\cos u = \sin 2u\), once with \(u = \frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\) and once with \(u = \frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\).

Denominator
\[\sin\alpha\cos\alpha - \sin\beta\cos\beta\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(\sin 2\alpha - \sin 2\beta)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\]
\[= \cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\]
Why: \(\sin u\cos u = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2u\); then \(\sin P - \sin Q\) with half-sum \(\alpha + \beta\) and half-difference \(\alpha - \beta\).

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)}{\cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)}\]
\[= \tan(\alpha + \beta) = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\) cancels (assumed non-zero), and \(\frac{\sin}{\cos} = \tan\).
